name: Omena Curry Stew
desc: Authentic Lake Victoria Omena stew gently simmered with tomatoes, onions, garlic, and coconut milk for optimal nutrition and rich flavor.
instructions: Wash Omena thoroughly in hot lemon water twice to remove sand and bitterness, then drain.
Heat oil in a pan and deep fry Omena lightly until crispy, then set aside.
Sauté onions, garlic, and ginger until fragrant.
Add tomato puree and simmer until thick sauce forms.
Stir fried Omena and coconut milk into the sauce, simmer for 10 minutes on low heat.
Serve warm with brown ugali and traditional greens.

name: Authentic Kenyan Githeri Special
desc: Nutritious traditional Kenyan corn and bean stew sautéed with fresh tomatoes, onions, and coriander.
ingredients: 2 cups boiled red beans or rosecoco
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and sauté onions until golden brown.
Add diced tomatoes and salt; cook until soft and saucy.
Stir in the pre-boiled maize and beans thoroughly.
Simmer on low heat for 15-20 minutes to absorb all flavors.
Garnish with coriander and serve hot with sliced fresh avocado.

name: Tilapia Stew with Coconut Milk & Managu
desc: Pan-seared fresh whole tilapia fish simmered in rich coconut stew, accompanied by steamed nightshade greens.
instructions: Pan-fry or grill tilapia lightly until golden skin forms.
Prepare a tomato-onion garlic sauce with coconut milk base.
Steam managu greens separately with a pinch of sea salt.
Simmer tilapia in coconut stew for 10 minutes.
Serve hot alongside warm brown ugali and steamed managu.

name: Fermented Sorghum Uji with Honey & Ginger
desc: Probiotic-rich fermented millet and sorghum porridge sweetened naturally with raw honey and fresh ginger.
instructions: Mix sorghum flour with 1/2 cup cold water to form a smooth paste.
Bring 2.5 cups of water with grated ginger to a boil.
Whisk in the sorghum paste continuously to prevent lumps.
Simmer gently for 10-12 minutes until thick and glossy.
Stir in honey and lemon before serving warm.

name: Traditional Mukimo with Sweet Corn & Kahurura
desc: Classic Central Kenya mashed dish made of soft potatoes, green peas, maize, and pumpkin leaves (kahurura).
instructions: Boil potatoes, green peas, sweet corn, and pumpkin leaves together with salt until soft.
Drain excess water, keeping 1/2 cup for mashing consistency.
Mash thoroughly until uniform and vibrant green.
Sauté onions separately until golden brown, then fold into the mashed mukimo.
Serve warm with beef stew or vegetable gravy.

name: Kienyeji Chicken Stew (Indigenous Free-Range)
desc: Slow-cooked indigenous organic chicken stew infused with garlic, ginger, tomatoes, and natural spices.
ingredients: 1 full Kienyeji chicken, cut into pieces
instructions: Boil chicken pieces with salt, garlic, and ginger for 35 minutes until tender.
In a separate pot, sauté onions in oil until caramelized.
Add tomato puree and spices, cooking down to a rich gravy.
Add boiled chicken along with its stock to the gravy.
Simmer for 20 minutes on medium-low heat until flavors integrate.
Garnish with fresh dania and serve with brown ugali.

name: Coconut Ndengu Stew (Green Grams Curry)
desc: High-protein green grams simmered in aromatic coconut cream with turmeric, garlic, and sweet bell peppers.
instructions: Sauté onions and bell pepper in oil until softened.
Add tomatoes, curry powder, and turmeric; cook into a paste.
Add pre-boiled green grams and stir well.
Pour in coconut milk and 1/2 cup water, simmer for 15 minutes.
Serve hot with chapati or rice.

name: Matoke & Beef Stew (Plantain Stew)
desc: Savory green banana (matoke) stew cooked with tender beef chunks, carrots, and sweet bell peppers.
instructions: Boil beef cubes with salt until tender.
In a deep pot, sauté onions, add tomatoes and carrots.
Add peeled green bananas and tender beef cubes.
Pour beef stock, cover tightly, and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes until matoke is soft.
Serve warm as a complete single-pot meal.
